notes.meaning: Jesus warned the crowd of a terrible disaster coming upon Jerusalem. Usually, having children was seen as one of God's greatest blessings. In the coming crisis, mothers would suffer so terribly seeing their children starve and die that childless women would be considered fortunate.

The suffering during the city's fall would be so terrifying that people would wish to be buried alive. They would beg the mountains and hills to collapse over them to hide them from the terrible judgment. Seeking shelter under falling rocks shows the deepest kind of dread and despair.

Jesus used a common proverb comparing green wood to dry wood. Green wood is hard to kindle, while dry wood burns up quickly. If an innocent and holy person like Jesus suffered this way, a wicked nation would face far worse fire and ruin.

Two criminals were led out with Jesus to be put to death at a site named The Skull. Jesus was nailed to a cross between them, numbered among the worst lawbreakers. Even in this humiliation, Jesus was not a helpless victim, but freely laid down His own life.

While being nailed to the cross, Jesus prayed for His executioners and asked the Father to forgive them. He made excuses for their blindness, showing that the purpose of His dying was to purchase pardon for sinners. Meanwhile, the soldiers cast lots to divide His clothes, leaving Him stripped of everything.

The crowd stood watching while the Jewish leaders mocked Jesus. They challenged Him to rescue Himself if He really was the Chosen One of God. They failed to realize that it was precisely because He did not save Himself that He could save others.

The Roman soldiers joined in making sport of Jesus as He hung on the cross. They brought Him sour wine, which was their ordinary drink on duty. By holding the drink toward Him, they mocked His terrible thirst.

The soldiers dared Jesus to prove His royal claim by freeing Himself from the cross. Because the Romans executed Him as an alleged rebel king, they turned His title into a cruel joke. They did not grasp that His true kingdom was not of this world.

A sign was nailed above Jesus stating the charge against Him: THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS. It was written in Greek, Latin, and Hebrew so that all the visitors in Jerusalem could read it. Even though Pilate posted it as a crime, God used it to proclaim Jesus' real authority in the main languages of the day.

One of the dying criminals joined the crowd in heaping insults on Jesus. He demanded that Jesus prove He was the Messiah by getting them all down from their crosses. Even in the face of death, this man stayed hard-hearted and only wanted to escape physical pain, not his sins.

The other criminal scolded his companion, asking why he had no fear of God when he was about to meet his Judge. He confessed that their own death sentences were entirely fair because of their crimes. At the same time, he declared that Jesus was completely innocent and had done nothing wrong.

The repentant criminal asked Jesus to remember him when He entered His royal rule. While everyone else saw only a dying man in utter disgrace, this man saw a King who held power over the life to come. He showed amazing faith by asking for nothing more than Jesus' favor beyond the grave.

Jesus promised the man that they would be together in paradise that very day. Paradise describes the place of rest and joy where the righteous go when they die. This shows that the souls of believers go directly to be with Christ after death, and that no sinner is beyond the reach of God's mercy.

differ.view: The criminal was saved by faith alone without water baptism or joining an earthly church, showing that physical sacraments are not strictly required for salvation.
The thief was saved by the same Word of promise given in baptism, since not having the chance to be baptized does not bring condemnation.

notes.meaning: Around noon, a deep darkness fell across the whole land and lasted until three in the afternoon. This darkness was not an ordinary eclipse, because the Passover occurred during a full moon. God sent this midday gloom to mark the awful weight of the judgment Christ was bearing.

As the sunlight failed, the large curtain inside the temple tore right down the middle. This curtain had separated the people from the Most Holy Place, where God's presence rested. The tear showed that Jesus' death took away the old barriers, opening free access to God for all believers.

Jesus cried out with a clear, loud voice, placing His spirit into His Father's care before breathing His last. Because He was sinless, death had no rightful power over Him; He chose to hand over His life of His own free will. He died with the words of scripture on His lips, showing complete trust in His Father.

The Roman officer in charge of the execution watched everything that happened and gave glory to God. Seeing Jesus' peaceful surrender and the wonders in the sky, he was convinced that Jesus was innocent. He openly declared that Jesus was truly a righteous man.

The crowds who had come out to watch the crucifixion walked home beating their chests in deep distress. The darkness and the strange manner of Jesus' death shook their consciences with fear. They realized that a terrible crime had been committed and feared that God's judgment would fall.

Jesus' close friends and the women who had traveled with Him from Galilee watched these events from a distance. Fear kept them from standing near the cross, but their deep love kept them from walking away. They stood watching with heavy hearts, unable to understand what had taken place.

A respected member of the Jewish high council named Joseph came forward. He was a good and upright man from the town of Arimathea who lived in hope of God's coming kingdom. When the council plotted to murder Jesus, Joseph had refused to agree with their plan.

Joseph went directly to Pilate, the Roman governor, and asked for Jesus' body. As an influential leader, he used his standing to gain legal custody of the Lord. He wanted to ensure that Jesus received an honorable burial instead of being thrown away with common criminals.

Joseph took Jesus down from the cross, wrapped the body in clean linen cloth, and laid Him in a tomb cut into solid stone. This grave had never been used before, which honored the Lord's body. God raised up a quiet follower to care for Jesus when the other disciples were absent.

The burial was completed on the Preparation Day, just as the Sabbath was beginning at sunset. Jewish days began at dusk, so the workers had to finish their task quickly before the time of rest started. They ordered their affairs with haste so they would not violate the holy day.

The faithful women who had come with Jesus from Galilee followed Joseph to the tomb. They watched carefully to see the exact location of the gravesite and how Jesus' body was placed inside. Their devotion to Jesus drove them to stay close to the very end.

The women went home and prepared fragrant spices and perfumes to treat Jesus' body after the holy day passed. Then they stopped all their work and rested on the Sabbath to obey God's law. Their love moved them to prepare for anointing Him, but their reverence for God led them to keep His day of rest.
